## Ontario Security Deposit Dispute: Practical Next Steps

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg

You have a solid fact pattern to organize: written lease, move-out photos, no documented damage beyond normal wear, and a deduction notice sent 18 days later. The safest approach is to build a clean paper trail, request repayment in writing, and prepare for Ontario’s tenant-dispute process if needed.

## Action Checklist for Deposit Recovery

| Step | What to do | What to keep |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Gather the lease, move-out date, and deposit payment proof | Signed lease, receipts, bank transfer, e-transfers |
| 2 | Save move-out evidence from 2026-02-15 | Photos/videos, timestamps, witness names, final cleaning records |
| 3 | Organize the landlord’s deduction notice | Full notice, date received, itemized deductions, any text/email messages |
| 4 | Compare the claimed damage to normal wear | Notes showing no pre-existing damage report or no move-in condition form |
| 5 | Send a short written demand for the withheld amount | Copy of your message, delivery proof, reply from landlord |
| 6 | Set a response deadline | A clear date by which you want repayment |
| 7 | Escalate if the landlord refuses | Ontario tenant board/tribunal filing info, filing dates, fee receipts |
| 8 | Keep one master timeline | Move-in, move-out, notice date, follow-ups, any inspections |

## Documents to Gather Before You Send Anything

- Signed lease and any addenda
- Proof of deposit payment
- Move-in condition report, if one exists
- Move-out photos and video from 2026-02-15
- Dated screenshots of messages with the landlord
- Deduction notice received 18 days after move-out
- Repair invoices or estimates the landlord sent, if any
- Your own written notes on the condition of the unit
- Witness statements, if someone saw the condition at move-out
- Forwarding address and proof you provided it
- Any cleaning receipts or contractor receipts, if relevant

## Concise Draft Message to Request Return of the Deposit

Subject: Request for Return of Withheld Deposit

Hello [Landlord Name],

I am writing about the deposit withheld from my tenancy at [address]. I moved out on 2026-02-15, and I do not agree with the deduction notice I received 18 days later.

I left the unit in good condition, with only normal wear and tear, and I have move-out photos from the day I vacated. I have not been provided with documentation showing damage beyond normal wear or a valid basis for the amount withheld.

Please return the withheld portion of my deposit within **7 days** of this message. If you believe any deduction is justified, please send:
- an itemized breakdown,
- supporting photos or invoices,
- and the specific reason each deduction was made.

I would prefer to resolve this directly and promptly.

Regards,
[Your full name]
[Phone number]
[Email address]

## Preparation Tips That Help Your Position

- Keep your message calm, factual, and short.
- Attach only the strongest evidence first: move-out photos, lease, and the deduction notice.
- Use one timeline document so dates stay consistent.
- Avoid arguing by phone only; follow every call with a written recap.
- If the landlord responds, save the reply exactly as received.
- If you file a claim, use the same facts and documents you already organized.

## Sources

- Ontario government tenancy information: https://www.ontario.ca/page/renting-ontario-your-rights
- Landlord and Tenant Board: https://tribunalsontario.ca/ltb/
- Residential Tenancies Act, 2006: https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/06r17
